request: Analyze GSE199429 for PMID 36780527 (Time of day determines postexercise metabolism in mouse adipose tissue.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Ribo-Zero Gold, NextSeq500 38-bp PE) of inguinal WAT (S3.5.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: male C57BL6/JBomTac mice, iWAT collected immediately (0 h) after 1-h maximal treadmill exercise or sham at ZT3 (early rest) or ZT15 (early active); n = 6 per group, 4 groups, 24 libraries (S3.1.p1, FIG1, S1.2.p1)
final.primary_estimand: acute exercise (RUN vs sham SED) effect on iWAT gene expression immediately post-exercise, estimated separately at ZT15 (early active) and ZT3 (early rest)
planned_contrasts: RUN vs SED at ZT15 (early active) (S1.2.p1; paper: 121 DEGs, mostly up)
RUN vs SED at ZT3 (early rest) (S1.2.p1; paper: 0 DEGs)
ZT15 vs ZT3 in SED (time-of-day, sedentary) (S1.2.p1; paper: 192 DEGs)
ZT15 vs ZT3 in RUN (time-of-day, exercised) (S1.2.p1; paper: 744 DEGs)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (independent animals, one sample per mouse)
final.normalization: edgeR filterByExpr (min count 10, design by group), TMM/CPM (S3.6.p1)
final.paper_method: edgeR quasi-likelihood NB GLM, design ~0 + group (4 groups) (S3.6.p1)
final.paper_results: 121 DEGs RUN vs SED at ZT15, 0 at ZT3; 192 time-of-day DEGs in SED, 744 in RUN; named up genes at ZT15 exercise: Nr4a1, Nr4a3, Vegfa, Adrb2, Cpeb2, Cyp2b10, Pdk4, Slc25a25, Ppargc1a, Ucp1, Dio2, Gadd45g, Irf4, Zfp516, Crem (S1.2.p2, FIG2); GO MF enrichment of DNA-binding transcription activator activity, steroid hormone receptor activity, glucocorticoid receptor binding (S1.2.p2)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S3.6.p1 gives the DE route (edgeR QL, ~0+group, filterByExpr min count 10, FDR 0.05, no fold-change rule). S1.2.p1 gives the four contrasts and their counts. S3.1.p1/FIG1 give the 2x2 design with n = 6 per group at the 0 h time point. The fasting experiment (S1.4) is qPCR only and not in GEO.

ownership.reasoning: Accession, tissue, sex, strain, design and n per group all match the paper.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (e.g. 13RUN_E) equal metadata titles (13Run_e) up to case; inspect reports 24/24 matches with normalize_keys. ex and time copied from GEO characteristics; grp is the paper's 4-level group (SED_ZT3, RUN_ZT3, SED_ZT15, RUN_ZT15). The _m/_e title suffix agrees with ZT3/ZT15 (morning/evening).

matrix.reasoning: GEO data_processing: 'processed.data.csv contains cpm after filtering by expression with cutoff at 10 counts'. Profile agrees: 0.17% integers, column sums 0.84-1.19 million (CPM, likely TMM-scaled), max 78k, no negatives, 16,233 Ensembl genes already filtered. Linear normalized expression, not counts. The paper's input was featureCounts raw counts (S3.6.p1), which were not deposited (supplementary_file NONE for samples). Library sizes are not deposited either, so counts cannot be recovered and must not be reconstructed.

final.analysis_type: factorial 2x2 cell-means (exercise x time of day), independent animals
final.formula: ~ 0 + cell (cell = ex x time, equivalent to the paper's ~0 + group)

design.reasoning: The paper fits one model on all four groups (S3.6.p1 ~0+group) and reports the exercise effect within each time of day plus the time-of-day effect within each exercise state (S1.2.p1). The exercise-effect contrasts answer the request; the time-of-day ones reproduce the paper's other reported counts. The exercise x time interaction (difference of exercise effects) is implied by the paper's claim of a timing-specific response but was not tested as such; it runs as exploratory from the same model. Pooling ZT3 and ZT15 into one RUN vs SED contrast is rejected because the paper's estimand is time-specific.

candidates.value: pooled RUN vs SED ignoring time
candidates.reason_rejected: the paper's estimand is exercise effect per time of day; pooling mixes the two phases
the paper fits one ~0+group model on all 24 samples

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: excluded: constant (all male); the GEO filterByExpr call's '+ sex' term cannot apply

covariance.reasoning: One iWAT sample per independent mouse; no subject, batch, or lane column in GEO. S3.1.p1 says the 0 h protocol was repeated in a subset of 24 mice; which cohort each library came from is not recorded, so a cohort term cannot be modelled (caveat). The paper's model has no covariates.

final.method: limma (moderated t, empirical Bayes) on log2(CPM+1), joint cell-means model

paper_route.method: edgeR QL NB GLM on raw counts, ~0 + group
paper_route.reason: GEO deposits only filtered CPM; raw counts and library sizes are not available, and CPM must not be converted back into integer counts

deviations: limma on log2(CPM+1) instead of edgeR QL on counts
filtering taken as deposited (authors' filterByExpr); no further filter

method.reasoning: Matrix policy: linear normalized expression -> log2(x+1) then limma. The joint limma executor fits ~0 + cell on all 24 samples, the same parameterization as the paper, so each contrast shares the variance prior over all groups as in the paper.

threshold.reasoning: S3.6.p1: all P values FDR-adjusted, alpha 0.05; no fold-change rule. Applied on the limma deviation route, BH within each contrast.

caveats: Paper's edgeR QL on counts could not run; limma on log2(CPM+1) from the deposited CPM is a declared deviation, so DEG counts are not expected to match exactly.
Cohort of origin (original vs repeated 0 h subset, S3.1.p1) is not recorded in GEO and cannot be modelled.
GEO processing notes (STAR 2.7.2b, Ensembl release 99, filterByExpr min.count 15 with + sex) differ from the paper's Methods (STAR 2.5.3a, release 92, min count 10).

study.reasoning: Paper route blocked by missing counts; thresholds and contrasts follow the paper.
